author: high
claim:
Let (G=(X\sqcup Y,E)) be a finite bipartite graph. For (S\subseteq X), let

\[
N(S)=\{y\in Y: \text{(y) is adjacent to at least one vertex of (S)}\}.
\]

Prove that (G) has a matching saturating every vertex of (X) if and only if

\[
|N(S)|\ge |S|
\]

for every subset (S\subseteq X).
evidence:
Proof. Write N_G(A) for the neighborhood in G when another graph is also under discussion.

First suppose M is a matching saturating X. For each x in X, let m(x) be the Y-endpoint of the unique edge of M incident with x. The map m:X→Y is injective because distinct edges of a matching have no common endpoint, and m(x) belongs to N_G({x}). Hence, for every S⊆X, m(S)⊆N_G(S) and |N_G(S)|≥|m(S)|=|S|.

Conversely, assume |N_G(S)|≥|S| for every S⊆X. We prove by induction on n=|X| that G has a matching saturating X. If n=0, the empty matching does so. Assume n>0 and that the assertion holds whenever the left part has fewer than n vertices.

Case 1: there is a nonempty proper subset A⊂X with |N_G(A)|=|A|. Let G_1 be the subgraph induced by A∪N_G(A). For every B⊆A, every G-neighbor of B lies in N_G(A), so N_{G_1}(B)=N_G(B), and therefore |N_{G_1}(B)|≥|B|. Since |A|<n, induction gives a matching M_1 in G_1 saturating A.

Let G_2 be the subgraph induced by (X\A)∪(Y\N_G(A)). For T⊆X\A,
N_{G_2}(T)=N_G(T)\N_G(A). Moreover,
N_G(A∪T)=N_G(A)∪N_G(T)
is the disjoint union of N_G(A) and N_G(T)\N_G(A). Consequently,
|N_G(A)|+|N_{G_2}(T)|=|N_G(A∪T)|≥|A∪T|=|A|+|T|.
Because |N_G(A)|=|A|, this yields |N_{G_2}(T)|≥|T|. Since 0<|X\A|<n, induction gives a matching M_2 in G_2 saturating X\A. The vertex sets of G_1 and G_2 are disjoint on both sides, so M_1∪M_2 is a matching saturating X.

Case 2: no nonempty proper subset A⊂X satisfies |N_G(A)|=|A|. Since the assumed inequalities are integral, every nonempty proper A⊂X then satisfies |N_G(A)|≥|A|+1. Choose x∈X. Hall's inequality for {x} gives N_G({x})≠∅; choose y∈N_G({x}). Let G' be the subgraph induced by (X\{x})∪(Y\{y}). For T⊆X\{x}, if T=∅ then its neighborhood is empty. If T≠∅, then T is a nonempty proper subset of X, so
|N_{G'}(T)|=|N_G(T)\{y}|≥|N_G(T)|−1≥|T|.
Thus G' satisfies the same neighborhood condition. By induction, it has a matching M' saturating X\{x}. No edge of M' meets y, so M'∪{xy} is a matching saturating X.

The two cases exhaust all possibilities, proving sufficiency and hence the equivalence.

glossary.X: the left vertex class of G
glossary.Y: the right vertex class of G
glossary.N_G(A): the set of vertices in Y adjacent in G to at least one vertex of A
glossary.G_1: the subgraph of G induced by A union N_G(A)
glossary.G_2: the subgraph of G induced by (X minus A) union (Y minus N_G(A))
glossary.G': the subgraph of G obtained by deleting x and y
